title: Tiered Retention + Compliance Assurance + Assured SLA playtest
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Run a three-armed pricing and feature-gating experiment bundling configurable observability retention, a Compliance Assurance pack, and an Assured SLA product to evaluate willingness-to-pay, procurement friction, and operational overhead for enterprise customers.
problem_statement: Customers asking for longer observability retention, formal compliance guarantees, and predictable latency/uptime are creating bespoke contracts which increase sales cycle and operational risk. We lack a standardized add-on that balances revenue, legal exposure, and implementation cost.
objectives: 1) Determine price elasticity and conversion lift for retention and compliance add-ons. 2) Validate a standardized Assured SLA offering (financially-backed) with acceptable operational limits. 3) Identify gating rules that minimize legal/security review while maximizing ARR.
hypotheses: H1: A configurable retention add-on (30/90/365 days) will convert 8-12% of MAUs on Enterprise trial into paid addon users within 60 days.
H2: Packaging Compliance Assurance (SOC2 + KMS integration + data residency options) as a single add-on reduces procurement time vs bespoke contracts by ~40%.

H3: Offering an Assured SLA (99.9% availability + p99 latency guardrails) at a clear price point will be purchased by <5% of customers but will increase average contract value (ACV) for those accounts by >20%.
H4: Entitlement gating via Console + feature flags prevents accidental exposure and keeps support load neutral (<10% increase in ticket volume).
planned_experiments: Experiment A (Retention Flex): Offer three retention tiers as add-ons - Bronze (30 days, $0 baseline), Silver (90 days, +$0.06/GB-month), Gold (365 days, +$0.18/GB-month). Measure upgrade rate, revenue, and query-cost impact.

Experiment B (Compliance Assurance Pack): Single SKU including SOC2 attestation, KMS/HSM key management integration, quarterly compliance report, and a compliance onboarding checklist. Price as a per-tenant add-on at $1,500/month plus $0.01/GB of retained telemetry.

Experiment C (Assured SLA): Two flavors - Standard Assured (99.9% uptime, 50ms p99 latency target, no rebate) and Premium Assured (99.95% uptime + 20% rebate on overage if SLA breached). Price Premium at +15% of base contract or as a fixed $5,000/mo for smaller accounts.
Experiment D (Bundled Offer): Combine Silver retention + Compliance Assurance as a 'Compliance+Retention' bundle with a 12% bundle discount to test if bundling increases take rate vs separate SKUs.

Experiment E (Gating Rules): Gate availability by customer tier and account risk score: enable for Enterprise accounts with completed security questionnaire and legal pre-approval; pilot for self-serve accounts via a 30-day trial cap.
Experiment F (Sales Motion): Run an outbound pilot with 12 strategic named accounts (existing prospects in negotiations) to test procurement speed and negotiate early adopter credits.
pricing_matrix_notes: We will A/B test both per-GB-month and per-tenant fixed pricing for retention and compliance. Initial anchors are conservative to reduce procurement objections; final pricing will adjust to observed willingness-to-pay. Finance sign-off required before public rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Week 0-2: Legal & Security finalize template terms and KMS integration checklist. 2) Week 2-4: Implement feature flags, billing SKUs, and Console UI for purchase. 3) Week 4-8: Launch internal pilot with Solutions Engineering and 12 named accounts. 4) Week 8-12: Open opt-in to Enterprise self-serve customers and run targeted pricing A/B. 5) Week 12+: Evaluate metrics and decide scale/retire variants.
acceptance_criteria: Operational: Billing SKUs functional, Console UI to purchase and view retention usage, feature flags in place.
Legal/Security: Standard addendum for Compliance Assurance approved; KMS integration guide published.
Measurement: Instrumentation for adoption, revenue, support tickets, query-latency, and cost-to-serve is live.
Business: Minimum detectable uplift: >=6% conversion on targeted pilot and projected +$60k ARR from pilot accounts within quarter, or clear qualitative procurement time reduction.
SRE: On-call runbooks and capacity plan documented for retention storage growth scenarios.
success_metrics: Add-on take rate: percent of eligible accounts that purchase each addon within 60 days.
Incremental ARR: dollar ARR attributable to experiment variants in first 90 days.
Procurement velocity: median days to contract signature for pilot vs historical baseline.
Support impact: delta in support tickets attributable to the new SKUs (<10% acceptable).
System cost delta: observed per-GB serving/storage cost vs revenue (target >30% gross margin on addon feature).
Customer satisfaction: NPS/CSAT change for pilot accounts post-onboarding.
dependencies: Legal sign-off on Compliance addendum (target Week 2)
Security architecture review for KMS/data-residency options
Billing platform support for metered retention SKUs
Console UI changes and feature-flag framework
Instrumentation for telemetry retention usage and cost reporting
Solutions Engineering capacity for named-account pilot
risks_mitigations: Risk: Sales friction due to price anchor - Mitigation: offer time-limited pilot credits and an explicit ROI spreadsheet.
Risk: SLA liability exposure - Mitigation: cap financial exposure in SLA language and require legal approval per account for Premium Assured.
Risk: Increased storage/serve costs - Mitigation: conservative pricing, telemetry quotas, and pre-flight capacity validation.
Risk: Security/customer data concerns - Mitigation: require completed security questionnaire and limited rollouts for high-risk accounts.
Risk: Measurement noise - Mitigation: use control group and incremental attribution; run experiment long enough for signal.
notes: We intentionally price some variants conservatively to prioritize learning about procurement friction rather than revenue maximization in the pilot. Post-pilot, iterations will include targeted enterprise pricing and potential channel packaging for partners.
